findings.section: 4 DeviceLayout Cross-Check (Extrapolation rule; Fig. 2 caption; Table 3 footnote)
findings.evidence_span:
For the initial qubit,
the circuit-model cap of Section~\ref{sec:static} trims it at
$4.477$\,GHz.
findings.fix: Move the capacitance bound and circuit-model cap (Section 5) ahead of the cross-check, or introduce the cap in one sentence where Section 4 first uses it, since Section 4 and its figure/table already apply it.

findings.evidence_span:
caps the qubit at
$4.477$\,GHz ($+8.1\%$)
findings.fix: State the referent: "+8.1% above the published 4.14 GHz initial qubit frequency".

findings.evidence_span:
bracket
    the island capacitance $\Cisl$ of the unmodified device
findings.fix: Define "unmodified device" at first use (the initial design as published, meshed as the fixture), or use "initial design" throughout.

findings.evidence_span:
on the $h/2$ meshes of
Section~\ref{sec:crosscheck} the two codes solve the same discrete problem
findings.fix: Define the mesh level h (DeviceLayout's straight-sided mesh) and h/2, h/4 before the intro uses them, or gloss them where first used.

findings.evidence_span:
uniform ladders, in two refinement families (two ways of subdividing the
same starting mesh)
findings.fix: Add a short gloss of "ladder" (a series of uniformly refined meshes of one design) where first used; the definition does not come until Section 3.1.

findings.evidence_span:
Newton's method
in
DeviceLayout's variables meets the example's criterion in 3 or 4 Palace
runs with any of three Jacobians, against 10 to 12 for PRIMA
findings.fix: Gloss PRIMA (derivative-free optimizer used by the example), the "variables" and the three Jacobians briefly, or point to Section 6; the abstract uses them undefined.

findings.evidence_span:
at the
example's own discretization
findings.fix: Define "DeviceLayout's discretization" (curved mesh, p = 2) where first used; the term is defined only in Section 4 but Section 3.1 and Table 1 already rely on it.

findings.evidence_span: scaling law $\partial F_q/\partial x_1 = F_q/x_1$
findings.fix: Define F_q (the qubit component of the objective F) and f_h (geode-fem's p = 1 frequency on h) where they first appear.

findings.evidence_span: by about the charging energy $E_C/h$ (Section~\ref{sec:junction}).
findings.fix: Say in the footnote that E_C = e^2/2C_Sigma is the charging energy, or reword so the symbol is not used before Section 3.2 defines it.

findings.evidence_span:
Three checks
test the estimates: a second refinement family and Palace's adaptive
refinement (Figure~\ref{fig:initialq}; the adaptive runs check only the
qubit), and a common-limit fit.
findings.fix: Define "common-limit fit" (one limit and rate fitted to both element-order pairs) at this first mention; it is explained only in the last paragraph of the section.

findings.evidence_span:
Five words sort the evidence, and Table~\ref{tab:tiers}, in the
Discussion, sorts every result by the tiers they name.
findings.fix: The paragraph names four tiers (Bounded, Model-dependent, Estimated, Computed), five words, while Table 6 has six rows (adds Consistency, Not claimed). Reconcile the count and say what the extra rows are.

findings.evidence_span: The brackets are the only bounds, and the cap follows from a bracket
findings.fix: Use one term for the two-sided capacitance result: "bracket", "bound", "two-sided bound" and "bounds" alternate. Also note "band" (extrapolation range) sits next to "bound" and is easily confused with it.

findings.evidence_span: The \emph{unmodified} device is the initial design as published
findings.fix: The same object is called the initial design, the unmodified device, and the fixture (a mesh of it). Pick one name for the design and keep "fixture" for the mesh only.

findings.evidence_span: eigenmode-participation (EPR) derivatives
findings.fix: Section 3 expands EPR as "energy-participation ratio"; use the same expansion in Table 6.

findings.evidence_span:
The
\emph{fixture} is a straight-sided mesh of the initial geometry
findings.fix: "fixture" collides with its ordinary software-testing sense; consider "reference mesh" or flag the usage.

findings.evidence_span:
\item \textbf{Same-input-mesh agreement with Palace}, with the
    $17.49$\,GHz mode
findings.fix: The agreement result is listed last but is Section 3, the first results section; reorder the contribution list to match (agreement, cross-check, bounds, re-optimization), and add a one-paragraph "Section N does X" roadmap.

findings.evidence_span:
Palace's
still-rising adaptive refinement puts the initial and final designs' qubit
frequencies $7.0\%$ and $8.0\%$ above their published values without
extrapolation.
findings.fix: The abstract and intro report adaptive refinement, extrapolations, bounds and caps before defining the designs, meshes and ladders they concern. Introduce the objects in a sentence or two ahead of the numbers.

findings.evidence_span:
Palace's own refinements of it move the qubit
from
$3.4527$ to $3.9528$\,GHz at $h_F/2$ ($+14.5\%$) and to $4.1721$\,GHz at
$p = 2$ on $h_F$ ($+20.8\%$)
findings.fix: Refinement results appear before the refinement ladders and the +x% convention are set up in Section 4; add a forward pointer or move this paragraph after the ladder.

findings.evidence_span: The rule was fixed after that static route was known
findings.fix: The caveat that the extrapolation rule was chosen after the static route was computed appears in full in the Introduction, Section 4, Section 5 and Table 6 (Consistency row); state it once in full and cross-reference it elsewhere.

findings.evidence_span:
estimates that lean low,
and
rest on Palace's finer levels
findings.fix: "Estimates lean low" and "adaptive runs are still rising" are restated at length in the abstract, intro, Sections 4 and 6, Table 6, the Discussion and the Conclusion; keep the full statement in Section 4 and leave one-clause pointers elsewhere.

findings.evidence_span:
Against the example's own objective, Newton's method in DeviceLayout's
variables reaches the criterion in 3 or 4 Palace runs with any of three
Jacobians, against 10 to 12 for PRIMA; geode-fem's shape derivative gives
no advantage here.
findings.fix: The Conclusion restates the abstract nearly verbatim (frequencies, 19--20%, 3 or 4 vs 10 to 12 runs); trim to the implication and the practitioner takeaway.

findings.evidence_span:
geode-fem's
shape derivative gives no advantage here.
findings.fix: The unprompted denial appears in the abstract, contribution list, Section 6, Discussion (its own paragraph), Table 6 "Not claimed" and the Conclusion; state it once in the results and once in the Discussion.

findings.evidence_span:
the independent solver geode-fem agrees
on shared meshes to $2\times10^{-4}\%$ (qubit)
findings.fix: The same agreement is quoted as 2x10^-4 % (abstract, Sections 4, 6, Discussion), 10^-4 % (Introduction, Section 4), 5x10^-5 % and 0.00005 (Section 3), and 6x10^-5 % (Section 3.2). Add one bridging sentence saying which level each number refers to, and use one rounding in the abstract and intro.

findings.evidence_span: The evidence places the $7$--$8\%$ shift in the discretization
findings.fix: The shift is quoted as 7.0%/8.0% (adaptive), 7.3--9.6% (extrapolated), 7.3--8.0% (initial), 8.7--9.6% (final) and now "7--8%". State which quantity "the shift" means or use the abstract's two figures consistently.

findings.evidence_span:
needs
a capacitor $19$--$20\%$ longer than published
findings.fix: The same headline is also quoted as 18.8% (step 2, 1446.078 um), +19.1%/+20.4%, +17% to +39% and +19% to +28% (bands). Add a one-line bridge in the abstract or Section 6 saying 19--20% is the two family estimates mapped by the scaling law and the others are different quantities.

findings.evidence_span: All six agree to $\leq 0.033\%$
findings.fix: The table's largest relative difference is 0.032% (resonator, which the abstract rounds to 0.03%); use a single value.

findings.section: Discussion (Why the shape derivative gives no advantage here)
findings.evidence_span:
A companion paper on adjoint shape
optimization of a conformal patch antenna
findings.fix: The patch-antenna comparison (38 parameters, CMA-ES, dB targets) is a dense tangent about a different problem inside the transmon story; shorten it to one or two sentences with the citation, or move it out.

findings.evidence_span:
Two solvers appear. Palace is the one the example uses; the second is
GEODE-FEM
findings.fix: The introduction is overloaded: it covers the transmon background, the published example, the second solver, the main result, the static route, the extrapolation-order caveat and the evidence vocabulary, with no roadmap. Split the result paragraph from the setup and add a short "why this exists / what each section does" paragraph.

findings.evidence_span:
A web search in October 2026 of the
complementary-bound and qubit-design literature
findings.fix: A literature-search methodology note interrupts the related-work paragraph, and Related Work sits between the introduction and the setup; consider moving it after the results or shortening the note.
